seasons.name: Spring
seasons.headline: Melons, mulberries and the last cool-season crops
seasons.blurb: Local farms bring in their final tomatoes, peppers and greens while melons and mulberries ripen. Outdoor markets are at their busiest before the heat arrives.
seasons.tip: Buy herbs as living pots now — kept out of the midday sun they crop for weeks.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.headline: Khalas dates, figs and greens grown under glass
seasons.blurb: It’s too hot for most field crops, so fresh dates, figs and okra lead the stalls, with hydroponic leaves from greenhouse growers. Many outdoor markets move to evenings.
seasons.tip: Shop early or in the evening, and bring a cool bag — or head to the air-cooled halls.

seasons.name: Autumn
seasons.headline: Planting time, pomegranates and the first local greens
seasons.blurb: As the heat breaks, farms replant and the first local leaves, herbs and chillies appear alongside pomegranates, guava and regional orchard fruit.
seasons.tip: Ask growers what they have just planted — it tells you what will be on the stalls in winter.

seasons.name: Winter
seasons.headline: The peak of Qatar’s growing season
seasons.blurb: The cool months are harvest time: local tomatoes, strawberries, cauliflower, carrots and cabbage, with outdoor markets open at their fullest.
seasons.tip: Weekend mornings are the best time to shop — go early for strawberries and fresh herbs.
